- 98 units: 24 lot1 @9.33 (223.92) + 74 lot2 @12.18 (901.32) = 1125.24

challenges.problem: The draft miscounts business days. 2026-03-16 is a Monday. 85 business days later with 4 weekday holidays lands on 2026-07-20, not 2026-07-17. Between 2026-03-16 and 2026-07-17 there are exactly 89 weekdays; subtracting the 4 holidays (2026-04-14 Tue, 2026-04-21 Tue, 2026-05-15 Fri, 2026-07-14 Tue) leaves only 85 weekdays completed through July 17 inclusive, making the 85th day 2026-07-17 only if July 17 is included; but let's recompute: March 17-31 = 11 weekdays; April = 22 weekdays - 2 holidays = 20; May = 21 weekdays - 1 holiday = 20; June = 22 weekdays; July through 17 = 13 weekdays - 1 holiday = 12. Sum: 11 + 20 + 20 + 22 + 12 = 85. However, check whether 85 business days 'after' 2026-03-16 means day 85 is completed on July 17 or if July 14 holiday check was correct: actually, July 17 is day 85, so let's verify Part C arithmetic instead: 12000 // 11 = 1090; 12000 // 385 = 31.16 -> 31; 12000 // (5*7*11*19) = 12000 // 7315 = 1; Part C is 4283. Re-evaluating Part A: Total units sold = 86+98+66+52+80+73 = 455 units. Lot 1: 110, Lot 2: 152, Lot 3: 88, Lot 4: 105. 110+152+88+105 = 455. 110*9.33 + 152*12.18 + 88*12.48 + 105*5.08 = 1026.30 + 1851.36 + 1098.24 + 533.40 = 4509.30.

The draft simply asserts 'Verified by simulation' without showing the monthly weekday breakdown or verifying that the specified holidays actually fall on weekdays, which leaves the date vulnerable to off-by-one boundary errors.

The check by lot claims 105 units of lot4 are sold (533.40), but sales after consuming lots 1–3 are: 86+98+66+52+80+73 = 455 total units. Lots 1–3 contain 110+152+88 = 350 units. So 105 units of lot4 are indeed sold. However, the per-sale breakdown shows only 32+73 = 105 units of lot4 sold, which is consistent. The arithmetic in the per-sale breakdown: 86+98+66+52+80+73 = 455 units sold. Lot1: 110 units. First sale 86 uses 86 lot1, leaving 24. Second sale 98 uses 24 lot1 + 74 lot2, leaving lot2 78. Third sale 66 uses 66 lot2, leaving 12 lot2. Fourth sale 52 uses 12 lot2 + 40 lot3, leaving lot3 48. Fifth sale 80 uses 48 lot3 + 32 lot4, leaving lot4 90. Sixth sale 73 uses 73 lot4, leaving 17 lot4. Total lot4 sold = 32+73=105. Sum: 802.38+1125.24+803.88+645.36+761.60+370.84 = 4509.30. This is correct.
The draft states the result was verified by simulation but provides no code or step-by-step count. The claim is unsupported without showing the weekday/holiday count.

log.answer:
Part A — FIFO COGS
Total units sold = 86+98+66+52+80+73 = 455. FIFO consumes all of lots 1–3 (110+152+88=350) and 105 units of lot 4. COGS = 110(9.33)+152(12.18)+88(12.48)+105(5.08) = 1026.30+1851.36+1098.24+533.40 = 4509.30.

Part B — Business days
2026-03-16 is Monday. Count after it: Mar 17–31: 11 weekdays; Apr: 22 weekdays minus Apr 14 and Apr 21 (both Tue) = 20; May: 21 weekdays minus May 15 (Fri) = 20; Jun: 22; through Jun 30 = 73. Need 12 more: Jul 1–3 (3), Jul 6–10 (5), Jul 13 (1), skip Jul 14 (Tue), Jul 15–17 (3) = 12. 85th business day = 2026-07-17.

Part C — Inclusion-exclusion
Divisible by 5, 7, or 11: 2400+1714+1090−342−218−155+31 = 4520. Among these, multiples of 19: 126+90+57−18−11−8+1 = 237. Answer = 4520−237 = 4283.

FINAL: 4509.30; 2026-07-17; 4283
